# Nested group visibility

Original XML fixture generated by `tools/hidden_group_fixture.py`, using the
repository's independently authored `shape-theme.docx` package scaffold and shape
helpers. No corpus document text or artwork is included.

Five rows have a visible green sibling and a nested group containing a red
rectangle plus a second-level blue rectangle. The nested group's `wpg:cNvPr`
hidden attribute is omitted, `0`, `false`, `1`, or `true`, respectively.

The reference application exports one page. Native PDF/PNG visual inspection shows
all three colors for the first three rows, and only the green sibling for the last
two. Hidden state suppresses the whole subtree without suppressing its siblings.
`cases.json` records positions and expected visibility; `hashes.json` identifies
source and native files. These artifacts establish drawing visibility, not all
editing or text-flow consequences. No reference/spec divergence is claimed.

The engine now retains each group's frame and omits descendants from the
rendering scene when hidden is true. The original XML remains intact through
editing/export and exact undo. Visible children still go through the ordinary
strict reader; unsupported content inside a hidden subtree is not loaded or
painted. Invalid boolean values remain errors. The tests compare all colored
regions with the native raster, including visible siblings and absent descendants.
This change is scoped to group visibility; independently hidden leaf drawings
are a separate supported-feature question.
